chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Samt who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The clean garment suppresses the enemy.'

key_terms.الثَّوْبُ النَّقِيُّ: Clean/pure garment — clothing maintained in a state of cleanliness and propriety
key_terms.الْعَدُوَّ: The enemy — can refer to external adversaries, the Devil (Shaytan), or the lower self
key_terms.يَكْبِتُ: Suppresses, humiliates, frustrates — conveys the idea of overpowering or causing shame to the enemy

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the effect of wearing clean clothes on one's enemies?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that wearing clean clothing has a spiritually and socially empowering effect — it suppresses and humiliates the enemy. In the early Islamic context, this teaching addressed both the physical dignity of the believer and the symbolic power that cleanliness and proper appearance carry in the face of opponents and adversaries, whether external enemies or the whisperings of Shaytan.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The clean clothes suppress the enemy’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jundab from Sufyan ibn al-Simt who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
Clean garments put down the enemy.’”
